cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 36th District in the U.S. House since 2015. Former Air Force JAG attorney and Reserve colonel, Ninth Circuit clerk and private-practice attorney. Previously served on the Torrance City Council, in the California Assembly (2005–2010) and in the State Senate (2011–2014).

endorsements.text: Endorsements listed for his 2026 race include the California Democratic Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and the Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Lieu on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, police pay and pensions, the Second Amendment, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We also found no statement from him on H-1B visas. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. The pages don't say where he was raised or what year he moved to California. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through the 118th Congress key votes, so later items on it were not read. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages available.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Houston Brignano

money.note: Individuals gave $7,020; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 36th Congressional District in 2026. Describes himself as a South Bay native and Marine veteran with two Iraq deployments. Lives in the South Bay with his wife and three homeschooled daughters. No elected office is listed.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed or recommended by April's Common Sense Cali Voters (a Sway voting group), Beverly Hills Moms (a Sway voting group) and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find his current occupation, his education, or any independent reporting confirming his birthplace or hometown. Beyond the Marine Corps service he describes, we found no work history, and no elected or appointed office. We found no documented positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, gun laws, or abortion. His stated views come only from his campaign site and one Ballotpedia survey. An 'Open Letter' on his campaign site was not readable, and we found no news coverage of controversies.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he is a South Bay native, born and raised there, and that he is raising his family in the South Bay. This is self-reported and not independently confirmed.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $7,020, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Marine Corps veteran with two Iraq tours, enlisted after high school. He serves on the boards of a homeschool co-op and a church, which do not count toward the score. No elected office, legislative, legal or policy career appears in the pages reviewed.
qual.why: He has military service but no governing, legislative, legal or budget experience in the record, which puts him in the low band for a first-time candidate.
qual.label: He has military service but no governing, legislative, legal or budget experience in the record, which puts him in the low band for a first-time candidate.

clean-money.evidence: Said he takes no corporate PAC money and will publish every meeting, every donor and every vote explanation online (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, 2025).

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said he would create innovation zones for technology, manufacturing and energy and streamline regulations that he says keep California's opportunity artificially constrained and costs high (Ballotpedia survey).

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said Americans should be trusted with choice in housing, healthcare and education (Ballotpedia survey). He gave no specific voucher, charter or teacher-pay proposal.
